title: A king’s pilgrimage may have lowered the price of gold in Cairo
body: Mansa Musa, ruler of the Mali Empire, passed through Cairo in 1324 on his way to Mecca with a vast caravan and a fortune in West African gold, which he gave away lavishly. The chronicler al-Umari wrote that gold lost value there for at least twelve years afterwards. Modern historians treat the reported size of the caravan as exaggerated, and some argue the dip was within normal price swings.

slides.prompt: Mansa Musa ruled which empire, and where was he heading in 1324?
slides.answer: The Mali Empire; to Mecca, on pilgrimage
slides.detail: He passed through Cairo with a vast caravan and gave away West African gold so lavishly that, the chronicler al-Umari wrote, gold lost value there for years.
